protocol: define no-op X509TrustManager.checkServerTrusted -> SSLContext.init(..., trustAllCerts, ...) -> Builder.sslSocketFactory(factory, ...) -> Builder.hostnameVerifier(alwaysTrue) -> build/use client
important_note: No canonical CrySL rule named TLSCertificateValidation was found in the consulted research. The requested raw primary URL reportedly returned HTTP 404, the JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src directory reportedly contained no such file, and repository file search reportedly found no match. Therefore this is an evidence-derived reconstruction from the reported v1.0.0 implementation and advisory record, not a verified TLSCertificateValidation CrySL contract. unverified.TLSCertificateValidation is a namespace sentinel included solely to satisfy the required qualified-type shape; it is not evidence that such a Java API type exists.

events.name: declare_no_op_server_trust_validation
events.condition: Observing a checkServerTrusted declaration alone does not satisfy the predicate. The predicate requires evidence that the effective X509TrustManager permits arbitrary relevant server certificate chains by returning normally on all paths, without delegated validation or CertificateException. The reported v1.0.0 Java source reportedly has an empty checkServerTrusted body.

events.name: initialize_tls_context_with_custom_trust_manager
events.condition: Observing SSLContext initialization alone does not satisfy the predicate. It requires source/data-flow evidence that the supplied TrustManager array contains the no-op X509TrustManager and that the resulting context socket factory is later installed on the relevant client.

events.name: install_custom_tls_socket_factory
events.condition: Observing an sslSocketFactory call alone does not satisfy the predicate, because custom factories may validate correctly. It requires evidence that the factory originates from the SSLContext initialized with the permissive manager and remains attached to the client used for the connection.

events.name: install_allow_all_hostname_verifier
api_patterns: public boolean verify(String hostname, SSLSession session)
events.condition: Observing a HostnameVerifier installation alone does not satisfy the predicate. It requires evidence that the installed verifier returns true for arbitrary hostname/session inputs on every effective path. In the reported v1.0.0 Java source, verify(String, SSLSession) reportedly returns true unconditionally.

events.name: build_configured_http_client
events.condition: Observing build() alone does not satisfy the predicate. It requires that the built instance retains the custom TLS configuration, is reachable from the reported method result, and is selected for an actual TLS connection.

semantic_scope: This is an evidence-derived, source-level detector reconstruction for the reported org.mifos.mobilebanking.api.SelfServiceOkHttpClient.getMifosOkHttpClient finding at source tag v1.0.0. It observes construction and installation of a permissive X509TrustManager-backed TLS socket factory plus an always-true HostnameVerifier on an OkHttp client builder. It is not a verified CrySL contract and does not itself observe a TLS connection.

detector_semantics.claim: The normalized advisory record claims that getMifosOkHttpClient installs an all-trusting X509TrustManager and a HostnameVerifier that always returns true, such that certificate-chain and hostname authentication are not performed by that client configuration.
predicates: An X509TrustManager implementation used by the SSLContext has an effectively no-op checkServerTrusted implementation.
The SSLContext is initialized with that manager and its SSLSocketFactory flows to OkHttpClient.Builder.sslSocketFactory.
The Builder installs a HostnameVerifier whose verify(String, SSLSession) result is unconditionally true.
The configured builder is built and the resulting OkHttpClient is the client selected for the connection.
limitations: No TLSCertificateValidation CrySL source or detector implementation was found, so predicate names and event order are not source-verified detector semantics.
The finding is a normalized advisory record, not a runtime trace.
Static source evidence cannot establish Android/OkHttp provider behavior for a particular deployed build, request path, or server certificate.

The overloaded OkHttp sslSocketFactory call reportedly receives the socket factory made from the custom SSLContext but separately receives a default X509TrustManager; version-specific OkHttp handling of that pairing requires compatibility evidence.

documented_behavior: Android documents X509TrustManager.checkServerTrusted(X509Certificate[], String) as building a certification path to a trusted root and returning only if that path is validated and trusted for server SSL authentication.
Android documents HostnameVerifier.verify(String, SSLSession) as returning true only when the hostname is acceptable.
The reported v1.0.0 source defines an empty checkServerTrusted implementation, initializes an SSLContext with that manager, and installs a verifier whose verify method returns true.
preconditions: The custom X509TrustManager must be the effective trust manager used by the TLS socket factory during the relevant handshake.
The built OkHttpClient must retain and use the installed SSLSocketFactory and HostnameVerifier.
The code path must execute in the deployed artifact, and the client must be used for a TLS request.
No subsequent configuration or transport selection may replace or bypass the relevant client configuration.
